_meta: One eval/experiment metric per unit, plus a pre-experiment covariate for the same unit. For each unit (a user, a task, a shard) x is a value measured BEFORE the experiment -- last week's score, the baseline-period metric -- and y is the metric measured DURING the experiment. The two are correlated because a unit that scored high before tends to score high now, for reasons that have nothing to do with the treatment. CUPED (Controlled-experiment Using Pre-Experiment Data) uses that correlation to remove the pre-existing, treatment-irrelevant variation from y: it forms an adjusted metric y' = y - theta*(x - mean(x)), where theta = Cov(x,y)/Var(x). The adjusted metric has the SAME mean as y (so it is unbiased and estimates the same quantity) but LOWER variance -- reduced by the factor (1 - rho^2), where rho is the correlation between x and y. Lower variance means a tighter confidence interval on the treatment effect, i.e. more statistical power from the same number of units. Every mean, variance, and correlation here is computed exactly.
